Participants:
Ria Strasser-Galvis, International Government Affairs, Google USAID Lead (Based in DC) Also working
with World Bank, IMF

SETTING THE AGENDA FOR THE DISCUSSION - KENNY
• Introductions
• We appreciate the efforts by Google to respond to this crisis through your support for humanitarian
organizations, as well as your actions to remove content that violates your Terms of Service and
promote more authoritative information. We also saw this week's statement announcing $10 million
in new funding-bringing you to $45 million-and providing details on your work with the IRC through
United For Ukraine.
• We'd liketo keep open lines ofcommunication with Google across any areas of mutual interest.
Today, however, we wanted to dive deep in a few areas, which we shared ahead of this call.
1) Discussing MDM and a Rapid Escalation Process for Content Moderation Concerns
2) Status Update on Google Productsin the Region and Alternative Content Delivery Methods

• For the Europe/Eurasia region, we have a trusted network of local partners (both media and

ASK: What is the application process by which the $10M funding is distributed? How
might we refer local partners to Google for further consideration?
• On research: There is an increased need to develop local research capacity to do this work in the
countries where USAID works. Capacity levels vary depending on where we work. But in some of
the countries that are the most vulnerable, USAID has contacts and potential partners that we could
recommend or do outreach to. We can also commit to providing some

needed for interested groups. We have a good ground-game and want to understand how we can

Some of the countries which have a high level of vulnerability, for example, to Russian

example, Central African Republic, Mali, Burkina Faso). The House has just passed

- Thank you for raising these concerns.
- Dis/misinformation is the core of what Google tries to address as an organization that
focuses on organizing trustworthy information. It's a core part of what they do - not on the
- They have developed systems overtime to measure and address information quality - they
uprank content to surface authoritative information and then downrank less authoritative
They elevate content from news organizations for trending events e.g. Covid.
They have policies that determine what is / is not allowed on the platform - content, user
behaviors - and are working to make those as clear and specific as possible.
- Constantly trying to adapt systems based on user flags/feedback and refinements to ML/AI
systems based on updates to their training data (e.g. content examples).
Policies pre-exist the Ukraine conflict. Bad actors are active before, during and after
conflict - have an evergreen approach.
Realize that these systems are imperfect. Very well funded actors (state / non state /
commercial / etc.) use Google to game their services, harm users, etc.
- They have two groups - Intelligence desks (track narratives / threats) and Threat Analysis
- They share relevant information through sister companies to address cross-platform
- The threat in Ukraine, Europe is not new -ongoing Russian aggression, manipulation of

Still mapping out potential partners for Trusted Flaggers, e.g. National Government, Local

- On Ukraine: Deplatformed state-sponsored media. Removed 60K videos. 40M views of

SERVICE AND PRODUCT AVAILABILITY - AMY
• Given the pace of the conflict and its many ripple effects, our partners are struggling to
understand which platforms are still available to publish and monetize their content.
• Like you, we want YouTube to remain online in Ukraine, Belarus and Russia as it is one of the
most effective ways for democratic actors to reach and engage their audiences.
• We are also aware that Google has temporarily paused ads and the monetization of content in
Russia through Google Display Network.
• So, we have two questions -
• ASK: Would it be possible to allow certain vetted partners - such as civil society
organizations and media outlets - to continue monetizing their content inside Russia?
Google Response: Clement
- Suspension of all ads was punitive towards any users. It was because of the financial and
political ecosystem. Not making exceptions because of constraints they face.
• ASK: Are you noticing any changes in userbehavior, such as platformhopping or
VPN use, and how canweshare those insights with our partners to pivot where they
are placing content? (PAUSE.)|
- No useful insights here that they could share with us. They follow open source reporting
on platform, VPN usage, etc.
• Moving forward, we want to be thoughtful partners and better understand the pressures and
tensions that you all are facing to keep YouTube online and moderate content in the region.
IN-KIND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE - AMY
• Shifting topics, we'd also like to take some time today to talk about in-kind technical assistance
in more depth...
• As you know, USAID works across government, civil society and the media. Our local partners
vary in their knowledge, experience and resources when it comes to working with search
engines, content streamingplatforms, advertising technology and cybersecurity tools.
• We want to recognize and appreciate the resources that Google has already made available,
through projects like Grow with Google, Google News Training Center, Google Skillshop, Analytics
Academy and the Advanced Protection Program.

•ASK: What is the best wayto start building relationships between our USAID Missions

Google Response: Clement, Alex and Ria
- Checkout this site. This is a good starting place in terms of ad credits.
- Some assistance is available through open calls (e.g. public Uls) others are more closed
processes (not scaled to the public).
- For example, they need to go through internal vetting for anyone who can see search
trends - these are usually the WHOs of the world.
They have trusted partners and use their trusted networks for more sensitive process/
data access e.g. Trusted Flagger Program.
They can help us connect people based in regions, but they may not be responsible for
making sure a partner gets through the vetting process.
Ria offered to verify open vs. closed processes and do training (ToT) for staff at USAID
Missions to help raise awareness about different types of in-kind assistance.
For the more closed processes, send requests / referrals to Ria, Alex, Clement, etc. to
make sure our partners are considered.
NEWS AND MEDIA - JOSH
• Can USAID refer more local Ukrainian, Belarussian and Russian newsrooms into the Google
News Initiative?
• USAID, for the Summit for Democracy, is supporting the Media Viability Accelerator (see fact
sheet from White House, Summit for Democracy deliverables).
• This will include a data architecture to get data on local media around the globe, to better
understand their business models, so that we can gain insight at scale on how local media
is adapting/surviving and so that local media can build their own solutions.
• We are supporting a coalition of media development organizations to develop this product
with an eye to have them maintain it / update it regularly.

• They (specifically Jason Lambert from Internews) have recently met with Ben Monnie from
GNI, because there are some similarities with the GNI/Financial Times Accelerator
• We know that these initiatives are quite different (we are targeting small, local media,
downstream from the kinds of media that GNI targets, and we are looking at creating
something that will regularly be updated), but are there ways we could develop a working
• Weare also working through MVA with Ads for News (WEF/GARM) and are looking to find
ways that we can direct more ad revenue to independent media. We appreciate what
Google has done with A4N (see background on p.5) and are looking for ways to scale up
to get more independent media in more countries where we work onto Google Ad
packages.
Google Response: Clement
- Doesn't have a ton of answers here.
- Typically training, support, etc. seems like there is overlap, but doesn't know where they
are on budgets, etc.
- Scaling up work on digital democracy; with events in Ukraine a lot of appetite to address digital
- A/AID announced this during S4D. 3 objectives (1) helping to really underscore consensus around
what digital democracy and what the standards are. Working in partner countries to align them with
regulatory principles.(2) Thinking about culture of rights respecting technology - tech code of ethics.
(3) civil society strengthening (4) establishment of multi-staeholder holder groups at country level.
Build connective tissue around rights respecting the ecosystem.
Google Response: Alex
This is very timely. Just spent the morning talking about Ottawa agenda.
Need to hold all stakeholder groups to account for what they do.
Let them know when we are ready to have more conversations around the pillars of ADD.
WRAPPING UP - KENNY
• IFTHERE IS TIME - I was speaking with one of our teams that is focusing on economic growth
and development in Ukraine. They were interested in the $5 million Google for Startups Ukraine
Support Fund to allocate equity-free cash awards throughout 2022. Would you be able to share
more about this by email? I'd like to connect you with them.

PROMOTING AUTHORITATIVE INFORMATION
7

• (March 1) Of course we are working to not just reduce the reach of unreliable information, but also
to make reliable and trustworthy information readily available. Our systems are built to prioritize the
most authoritative information in moments of crisis and rapidly-changing news. When people
around the world search for topics related to the war in Ukraine on Search or YouTube, our systems
prominently surface information, videos and other key context from authoritative news sources.
• (March 29) As an information company, we take our responsibility seriously to provide reliable,
trustworthy information to people when they need it. We saw how many Ukrainians turned to
Search to find up-to-date information, including where to find shelter or humanitarian aid, and relied
on air raid alerts on their phones. To help, we're also rolling out new features that enhance access
to trusted information, including Info Panels in local languages and Transparency Labels for
publisher content on YouTube.
One positive effort-though it only peripherally affects YouTube-is Google's new Auction Package for Ads
for News, which Google launched in summer 2021 to help advertising agencies and brands to place ads in
trusted local websites (which often struggle to attract digital advertising) across 30 countries. Trusted
organizations screenthese news websites to exclude platforms that traffic in disinformation and hate
speech that advertisers see as detrimental to "brand safety." Such programs can help keep crucial local
Internews is partnering with Google and the media investment firm GroupM on this initiative through the
Media Program in Ukraine, and we encourage Google to continue to expand this program to other countries
around the world where independent media struggle to compete in the ad market.
